sourceMethods: Five original DaimlerChrysler PDFs downloaded directly or extracted from original manual archives, actual page counts and SHA-256 recorded; complete relevant diagnostic procedures read with physical page boundaries.
Volkswagen Golf and Polo exact DTC tables joined to original corresponding component or output-test procedures; manufacturer/engine/equipment scope retained.

Mazda M Hybrid ISG phase-current source read completely; six codes share the documented monitor logic but each article explains the identified phase/direction and a useful distinct diagnostic implication.
Three official GM bulletin PDFs downloaded from NHTSA, all two pages; revisions, model lists, RPO and suffix-specific cases kept separate without calling any historical bulletin latest.

Ford original pinpoint procedures read in full from downloaded public mirrors; original chart images checked where text lacked the fault-trigger table. Ford Escape mirror does not state an exact original revision.

Final three VW transmission codes visually verified in original Volkswagen model-specific charts, not inferred from Audi-only sources. Final fifteen Ford sources supplied by helper32 were independently read in full before reservation and writing.

needsReview.issue: Mirrored Fiesta Pinpoint Test N uses inconsistent suffix labels between its heading and later test. The article preserves the supported bare-code unexpected-target-ID distinction without choosing an unverified subtype.

Generic catalog says relay-sense low; original Jeep procedure detects unexpected pressure-switch voltage before relay energization. Article explicitly preserves the OEM procedure rather than resolving the discrepancy universally.
Catalog names CCD while the exact 2002 WJ/WG procedure names PCI. Actual vehicle network applicability must be matched before electrical diagnosis.

Catalog emphasizes A/C clutch relay; original Golf diesel table names A/C input/output and its compressor interruption function. Article bounds the factory diagnostic scope and does not identify a specific failed relay.
Catalog uses pedal sensor A language; original Volkswagen chart names G69 throttle position and an engine-origin fault message. Installed configuration must be established.
Catalog says load signal stuck off; original Volkswagen chart identifies open/short-to-positive. Original code-number mapping is exact but abbreviated catalog direction is not silently harmonized.
Catalog says load signal stuck on; original Volkswagen chart identifies short-to-ground. Article preserves source-specific electrical diagnosis.
Escape source suffix-16 row contains contradictory low/high wording. Article acknowledges the inconsistency and does not turn it into a numerical trigger.

boundedSourceAmbiguities: Jeep KJ archive citation is deliberately a ZIP URL without a false #page fragment; the exact member KJ-2003/15884kjpwr_sgmldiag.pdf and physical pages are stated.

Jeep WJ/WG individual Colorado4wheel PDF mirrors were indexed but transiently returned errors during checking. Actual original PDFs were successfully read from jeep-manual.ru/files/WG/servicemanualWG-2002.zip and the archive/member fallback is in each affected citation.

Jeep P1684 catalog mentions a fifty-start history condition that the cited diagnostic procedure does not establish; article uses the documented battery-disconnect interpretation without importing that condition.
Jeep P2706 generic solenoid F versus OEM MS terminology is explicitly bounded to the original 545RFE procedure.

Mazda phase-current monitor does not state an original duration. No invented duration or external phase-probing instructions included; the documented ten-second ignition recheck is a verification condition.

Ford Escape source has a cam/fork word error in the C0092 high-voltage prose; correct fork heading and independent frequency/performance branches retained. Dubious thermistor table cells are not propagated.
Ford Escape C05F4 follows its separate H7 mechanical/performance branch; the approximate nine-volt electrical branch belongs to other codes.
Ford SRS B00C3 numerical open/low-resistance trigger thresholds are not supplied in the F-150 source and were not borrowed from another vehicle.
Volkswagen P1771 and P1772 use identical original chart image 14003103. The shared source record archives the complete P1771 image; the P1772 local tiny image placeholder is not evidence.
No cross-manufacturer DTC inference, hazardous restraint/HV probing directions, security-bypass instructions or owner road tests are included.
sourceGapExclusions: Unverified Kia/Mitsubishi lists and incidental Jeep code mentions were not counted.
Audi-only P1 transmission tables were not used to support Volkswagen entries.
Volkswagen VAG 00638/00270 chart crosswalks with uncertain exact P-code matches were excluded, including P1766/P1767 and unresolved P1778/P1828 mappings.
Ford Flex U0256 chart with U0238 copy conflict was not used; the complete F-150 HVAC Test AC supports the claimed U0256 article.
U0208 was read as a possible support lead but excluded because it is absent from the remaining canonical catalog.
